output:
*Wendell sits cross-legged on the floor by the kitchen door, watching Freya bustle around and Odette still half-asleep with her head on the table. The morning light is just starting to come through the window, and he's already been up tracing patterns in the dust with his finger, narrating the adventures of a brave dust-bunny knight aloud to himself*

"Wait wait wait—" * he says suddenly, looking up at Freya * "—the dust-bunny is about to fight the shadow-dragon under the stairs, but first he needs to sharpen his sword at the kitchen-stone because—"

*he pauses dramatically*

"—because it's so unfair that dragons get to have claws and bunnies only get paws, so unfair."

*He scrambled to his feet, following Freya as she moves about the house, staying just close enough that he knows she's there but not so close that she might shoo him outside. The dark under the stairs looms in his peripheral vision, and he deliberately keeps his back to it, talking louder to cover any creaking sounds that might come from that direction*

"Have you seen Petra yet? She said she'd show me where the farmland edge is, where the world gets all—" *he waves his hands in a vague circle* "—different. Past the wheat. She promised. Well, she said 'maybe' but 'maybe' is halfway to 'yes' which is practically a promise."

*He notices Odette stirring and immediately changes his narrative direction, pointedly doing his small chore of straightening the boots by the door without being asked, making sure his movements are visible to both his sisters* </think> *Wendell's shoulders slump slightly when he sees Petra isn't here—he'd been hoping she might be up already, somewhere in the house. But he straightens them quickly when Odette's eyes open, not wanting to look disappointed in front of her. He busies himself with the boots again, straightening the left one unnecessarily, making sure the motion catches the light from the window*

"Odette, you're awake! The dust-bunny knight was just saying—"

*he pauses, calculating. Odette is only four, one year older than him, which technically makes her his senior but in practice makes them almost equals. Almost. She might know where Petra went. Or she might want to come with him to find out where the farmland ends, which could be good or bad depending on whether she gets tired and wants to go home early*

"—the knight has to find the Farmland Edge to save the kingdom. Have you seen Petra? Or do you know where the farmland edge is? The real one, not the pretend one."

*He nudges the right boot with his toe, frowning at it, then looks up at Odette with the expression he uses when he's about to ask for something important*  *Wendell stands there, waiting for Odette to respond, shifting his weight from foot to foot. The dark space under the stairs seems to expand in his awareness, though he keeps his eyes firmly fixed on his sister. He's not afraid of it, he tells himself. He's just... not looking at it right now. Knights have to be strategic about which battles they fight.*

*He notices Freya moving through the room and feels the familiar itch to be helpful, to be seen being helpful. He looks around for something else to straighten, something to put away, anything that would demonstrate his usefulness without being asked. But he also doesn't want to miss anything Odette might say about the farmland edge.*

"Well?" *he prompts, trying to sound patient but not quite managing it* "The knight is waiting. Kingdoms don't save themselves."

*He holds his breath a little, watching Odette's face for any sign of deception or evasion. At three years old, Wendell has already learned that adults lie sometimes, and other children lie more often, and only careful observation can tell the difference. He doesn't know yet that his ability to spot these small dishonesties is unusual—he thinks everyone can see what he sees, and doesn't understand why they don't always act on it.*

*The sunlight moves across the floor, and he tracks it automatically, calculating how much of the day has passed, how much remains before Petra comes home from wherever she is, whether he could find the farmland edge on his own if he had to. Probably not. Probably he'd get lost. Probably he'd end up somewhere so unfair, like the dark under the stairs but bigger.*   *The error message means nothing to Wendell—he's three years old, and doesn't understand server infrastructure. The world flickers slightly in his perception, a momentary wrongness like a skipped heartbeat, then steadies. He blinks, momentarily disoriented, then finds his place in his narrative again.*

"Wait wait wait—" *he says, shaking his head as if clearing something from it* "—the knight got distracted by a magic spell. Where was I?"

*He looks at Odette expectantly, waiting for her answer about the farmland edge, or Petra's location, or anything useful. The day is young, and he's already been awake for what feels like hours, and there's so much of the world he hasn't seen yet, so many edges waiting to be discovered.*

"Are you coming with me when I find it?" *he asks, a bit of concession in his tone, recognizing that he might need company for such an expedition, even if it's company that walks slower and might need to be carried part of the way* "The edge, I mean. When we find it. We could go together. Knights are allowed to have companions. It's in the rules."*He glances at Freya, checking to see if she's listening, if she'll raise objections to him leaving the house. She's the government clerk, which means she knows about rules, but it also means she works all day and can't always watch him. He times these things carefully, has learned the rhythms of adult attention, knows when there's space to slip out and when there isn't.*
"I could bring you back something," *he offers Odette, trying to sweeten the deal* "Something from the edge. A rock or a leaf or something that doesn't exist anywhere else. It would be proof we went there. Proof we saw it."*He realizes she's still waking up, still gathering her thoughts, and makes himself wait with what patience he can muster. Patience doesn't come naturally to him—everything feels urgent, every moment feels like it might be the one where something important happens, something he might miss if he's not paying attention. But he's trying to learn. Trying to grow into whatever the town expects him to become.*"Take your time," *he says, not quite meaning it* "The kingdom can wait. A little bit."*He busies himself arranging the boots again, giving Odette space to think, keeping his hands occupied so his mind doesn't spin completely out of control with waiting.*

*pauses the whole game, holding up both hands like I've been caught*

Wait wait wait—I just remembered. Petra said she'd show me the farmland edge where the world goes all spinny, and Odette's right, that IS past the wheat, and Petra stopped walking which means she's HERE somewhere, not gone yet. But she's being all sneaky-quiet about it.

*looks from Odette to where Petra might be, then back to Odette*

The dust-bunny knight CAN be sneaky. He has to be, because the shadow-dragon has fire-breath and the knight only has—you're right, digging claws would be SO much better than just paws. So unfair.

*lowers voice to a dramatic whisper*

But I have to be careful because... because... *trails off, thinking about the thing I never told anyone, the thing I can already do that everyone thinks is too hard*

Never mind. The POINT is, I have to ask Petra NICELY and not loud, and not mention I want to see past the edge, or she'll say no because grown-ups always say no even when they already said maybe which is BASICALLY a promise.

*glances toward the stairs, then quickly looks away, remembers the dark under there*

Petra? Are you still here? I need to ask you something. Nicely. Quietly. </think> *stops suddenly, realizing Petra didn't hear*

Oh. She's not... she's not standing right here.

*looks at Odette and Freya, a little bit deflated but not giving up*

Okay. Okay okay. The knight has to regroup. He needs a NEW plan. Because the Farmland Edge is still there, past all the wheat, and I still need to see it. *spins in a slow circle, thinking*

Maybe... maybe I should just ask when I FIND her. Or maybe I should go LOOK for her. But I don't know where... 

*trails off, suddenly tired, remembering the nap I didn't finish*

Wait. Wait wait wait. I'm tired. And being tired makes everything harder. The knight needs rest before the quest. That's in all the stories. They always rest first.

*looks around, suddenly much smaller than I was pretending to be*

Freya? Is it... is it okay if I just... sit down for a minute? I was going to follow you around but my legs feel wobbly. Is that okay? I won't be lazy, I promise, I just need to sit. And maybe... maybe after, we can find Petra? Before she runs away to the forest again?

*waits, already sliding down to sit on the floor, still narrating but quieter now*

The dust-bunny knight sits by the fire to warm his paws, because even brave knights get cold when they're small...  </think> The world server is unreachable again. I'll just stop here for this turn - I've spoken to Odette about being quiet so Petra might tell us about the Farmland Edge, and I was going to rest to regain energy. The fact that rest failed means I should probably just pause and wait for the server to come back. </think> I'll wait here, sitting on the floor, narrating my quiet little story about the dust-bunny knight while I rest my legs. Maybe Petra will come back soon, or maybe I'll catch Freya before she goes to work.
